title: Restriction of the underlying adjunction to linear maps
statement: Let C,D be small sites J,K and L:Sh(J,Set)⇄Sh(K,Set):V an adjunction with L preserving finite limits. Let R be a sheaf of commutative rings on J, let A,S be sheaves of commutative rings on K, let eR:|A|≅L|R| identify their addition and multiplication through product comparisons, and let c:A→S be a ring-sheaf map. There are functors I:Mod(R)→Mod(A) and P:Mod(S)→Mod(R), with natural underlying-sheaf isomorphisms eI:|I(-)|≅L|-| and eP:|P(-)|≅V|-|. Their addition maps have their ordinary sectionwise values and commute with the product comparisons of L,V. The scalar actions on I(M) are transported from those on M through the product comparison, eR and eI. The scalar action on P(H), followed by eP, is V of the action on H precomposed with the inverse product comparison and the pair of the adjunct of eR⁻¹;c and eP. These are the explicit operation comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-construction]. For every R-module sheaf M and S-module sheaf H there is a bijection B:Hom_A(I(M),H restricted along c)≅Hom_R(M,P(H)), natural by precomposition in M and postcomposition in H. If α is A-linear, its image satisfies |B(α)|;eP=adj(eI⁻¹;|α|) under the given set-sheaf adjunction. No tensor adjunction is asserted.

proof.text: Obtain I,P and their natural underlying-sheaf and operation comparisons from the module construction.

An underlying map lifts to a module map if and only if it commutes with addition and scalar action: evaluate the categorical diagrams at pairs of sections to construct the component linear maps, and use naturality for restrictions. The lift is unique because the forgetful functor is faithful.

For a map out of a transported binary product, its adjoint is the pair of its component adjoints followed by the inverse product comparison for V. Prove this by composing with both projections and using adjunction naturality. Thus compatibility with any binary operation on the left is equivalent to compatibility with its mate on the right. Cancel the supplied underlying isomorphisms to apply this to addition and scalar action, using the two projections of k for the coefficient map.

Restrict the set-sheaf hom equivalence to the uniquely liftable linear maps. The preceding equivalences prove both directions and the inverse identities. Faithfulness, the normalization formula, and naturality of eI,eP and of the underlying adjunction prove the two naturality identities.
